description: The common build tool of the kit logic modules: compiles the source of a kit of your own (a folder with kit.json — { "schema": "gripforge.kit-module/1", "id", "version", "services"?, "requires"?, "optional"? } — and src/lib.rs giving "pub fn module() -> Rc<dyn KitModule>"; no Cargo.toml, no export macro) on the base GripForge fixes: the pinned Rust toolchain with its components, the locked crates, the options of each mode. Writes, per mode, <id>-<version>.<mode>.wasm and its manifest .kit.json (provides/consumes read from the binary, sha256), plus build.json; checks each binary against the base (its mode, its structures table, the links it takes). Both modes by default: "isolated" (a memory of its own) and "common" (relocatable, for a game that trusts the kit). Runs cargo locally: the first build of the common mode rebuilds the standard library (a minute or two). When the toolchain is missing the error gives the one rustup command to run (install: true runs it; it adds a toolchain beside the others and never changes the default one). Then declare a build with gripforge_third_party_kit_add. Guide: gripforge_docs { topic: "kit-third-party" }.

install.description: true: install the pinned toolchain with rustup when it is missing.

kit.description: Absolute path of the kit folder (kit.json and the Rust source).

mode.description: Which build(s) to make. Default: both.

out.description: Absolute path of the output folder. Default: <kit>/build.

sdk.description: Absolute path of the kit SDK: the kit-sdk folder of the GripForge CLI, or a GripForge checkout. Default: GRIPFORGE_KIT_SDK, else the SDK of the gripforge CLI found on PATH.

target_dir.description: Absolute path of the cargo target folder. Default: <kit>/target/gripforge-kit.

name: gripforge_third_party_kit_build
title: Build a kit of your own on the build base
